# Daily Papers
The project automatically fetches the latest papers from arXiv based on keywords.

The subheadings in the README file represent the search keywords.

Only the most recent articles for each keyword are retained, up to a maximum of 100 papers.

You can click the 'Watch' button to receive daily email notifications.

Last update: 2026-11-06

| **[4D Point Splatting for mmWave Radar Micro-Doppler Differentiable Rendering](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.08342v1)** | 2026-11-05 | <details><summary>Show</summary><p>Millimeter-wave radar resolves the micrometer displacements of a moving body as micro-Doppler, enabling gait, gesture, activity, pose and vital-sign sensing. Each task relies on a downstream model trained on real data, yet radar datasets lag orders of magnitude behind vision and language. Brute-force collection will not close that gap, and existing synthesis methods (forward-only simulators, learned generators and static-scene inverse renderers) cannot fit a real capture of a moving body, leaving a sim2real gap. We present 4D Point Splatting (4DPS), a physics-based differentiable renderer that fits an explicit moving scene to a real capture. Using the synchronized camera to initialize the room and body, we represent the scene as oriented points carrying material, normal and velocity, and splat each point into range and Doppler bins. Our output is the raw complex return a real radar records, so we apply the same signal processing on the rendered data to obtain any representation for training any SOTA downstream model. We fit 235 sequences on HuPR and 100 on RT-Pose, two datasets with different radars. Our reconstructions set the state of the art, with median correlations of 0.940 and 0.830 on range-azimuth, 0.829 and 0.695 on range-Doppler, and 0.988 and 0.966 on micro-Doppler. Our renders also set the state of the art in downstream sim2real gap. On RT-Pose, a pose model trained on them reaches 21.9 cm MPJPE on real data, against 16.7 cm for real training and 127.6 cm for the RF-Genesis baseline, where both the rendered- and real-trained models learn nearly the same features. Our custom CUDA kernels fit a sequence in 5.7 minutes on HuPR and 12.9 on RT-Pose on one H100, making dataset-scale inverse rendering of mmWave radar possible for the first time. This work can enable synthetic data generation for any human-centered downstream task and model, and scene editing for data augmentation.</p></details> | Under Review |
| **[Beyond Gait: Person Identification from Millimeter-Wave Point Clouds Across Activities of Daily Living](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.08818v2)** | 2026-11-05 | <details><summary>Show</summary><p>Person identification from millimeter-wave (mmWave) radar point clouds has primarily focused on gait. However, since indoor walking is typically brief and fragmented, gait-based identification is largely constrained to designated passages that support continuous walking. Meanwhile, non-gait activities of daily living (ADLs) are pervasive and also encode discriminative personal signatures. In this study, we evaluate the feasibility of ADL-based identification from sparse mmWave point clouds using mm-ADL, a dataset comprising seven core ADLs collected from 11 subjects under controlled protocols. Moving beyond uniform gait introduces significant activity-dependent variations that confound identity representations. To address this challenge, we systematically benchmark three activity-identity learning paradigms: monolithic learning, joint multi-task learning, and two-stage activity-conditioned routing, under both closed-set identification (ID) and subject-disjoint re-identification (ReID) biometric settings. In parallel, we propose Dual-Stream Static-Dynamic PointNet (DS-SDPNet), an architecture tailored to radar point clouds that captures complementary spatial morphology and motion dynamics. Across seven ADLs, DS-SDPNet achieves 70.2% mean closed-set identification accuracy and outperforms existing baselines on both mm-ADL and mmGait. Moreover, benchmarking the three paradigms without ground-truth activity labels during inference yields up to 68.0% closed-set accuracy and 75.4% ReID mAP, providing a systematic baseline and confirming the feasibility of point-cloud-based biometric identification across diverse daily activities.</p></details> | <details><summary>v2: R...</summary><p>v2: Revised the activity-identity learning framework, updated experimental comparisons, and improved manuscript presentation</p></details> |
| **[A Synchronized Tri-Modality Wireless System for Multi-Point Non-Contact Cardiac Monitoring](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.07358v1)** | 2026-11-05 | <details><summary>Show</summary><p>Cardiac physiological monitoring is fundamental to evaluating cardiovascular health and diagnosing related diseases. Non-contact radar sensing can capture chest-wall vibrations with spatial specificity, enabling localized physiological monitoring and cardiac assessment. Progress, however, has been limited by the absence of a reliable, research-grade hardware platform for rigorous validation of radar-based methods. Prior systems typically pair radar, namely Doppler cardiography (DCG), with only electrocardiography (ECG) or other coarse references, providing no direct mechanical ground truth and thus constraining fine-grained evaluation of radar outputs. We present a tri-modality wireless system that integrates ECG, seismocardiography (SCG), and DCG under a unified acquisition and control framework for time-aligned recording and analysis. The tri-modality system combines miniaturized wearable ECG/SCG modules with a high-resolution mmWave radar module, supporting spatially resolved sensing and subsequent feature extraction. To our knowledge, this is the first integrated ECG--SCG--DCG hardware system for comprehensive cardiac monitoring; it enables multi-point thoracic acquisition, achieves precise cross-modal synchronization, and maintains specifications suitable for wearable operation. Experiments on a linear-motion platform show close agreement between DCG- and SCG-derived displacements, confirming accurate displacement measurement. Human-subject studies further demonstrate cross-modal consistency and robust extraction of feature points, establishing ECG as the electrical anchor and SCG as the mechanical ground truth for DCG. Overall, the system provides a rigorous, spatially resolved validation platform that advances non-contact cardiac sensing and supports next-generation radar-based monitoring.</p></details> | 11 pages, 9 figures |
| **[MITO: A Millimeter-Wave Dataset and Simulator for Non-Line-of-Sight Perception](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.10259v4)** | 2026-11-05 | <details><summary>Show</summary><p>The ability to observe the world is fundamental to reasoning and making informed decisions on how to interact with the environment. However, optical perception can often be disrupted due to common occurrences like occlusions, which can pose challenges to existing vision systems. We present MITO, the first millimeter-wave (mmWave) dataset of diverse, everyday objects, collected using a UR5 robotic arm with two mmWave radars operating at different frequencies and an RGB-D camera. Unlike visible light, mmWave signals can penetrate common occlusions (e.g., cardboard boxes, fabric, plastic). MITO captures over 24 million mmWave frames and uses them to generate 550 high-resolution mmWave images in line-of-sight and non-light-of-sight (NLOS), as well as RGB-D images, segmentation masks, and raw mmWave signals, taken from 76 different objects. We develop an open-source simulation tool that can be used to generate synthetic mmWave images for any 3D triangle mesh. Finally, we establish benchmarks for NLOS segmentation and classification to demonstrate the utility of our dataset and simulator for enabling broader NLOS perception.</p></details> |  |
| **[Untangling Dense Crowds with mmWave Radar: From Crowd Semantics to Individual Spatial Behaviors](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.19357v2)** | 2026-11-03 | <details><summary>Show</summary><p>In this paper, we present a novel framework for recovering individual footprints and pedestrian spatial behaviors in dense crowds. This is a highly challenging problem, as pedestrians can merge or block one another often and for prolonged periods in crowded areas, leading to strongly entangled observations. Our approach jointly leverages learned crowd semantics and principled reasoning over persistent radar observability loss to systematically infer individual spatial footprints. At the macroscopic level, we learn spatial usage patterns of the crowd from radar point clouds, while at the microscopic level we develop a physics-informed model of radar observability loss caused by sustained merging and occlusion. Building on this macro-micro structure, we introduce a semantic-guided multi-hypothesis reasoning foundation that evaluates competing hypotheses via principled reasoning over many-to-one and one-to-none observation mappings, enabling untangling of individual spatial footprints. We evaluate the framework through 18 real-world experiments using an off-the-shelf mmWave radar, involving crowds of up to (and including) 10 individuals across six categories of diverse pedestrian behaviors, and four environments. Our methodology robustly recovers individual spatial footprints, even during prolonged and persistent observability loss, demonstrating strong structural consistency with the ground-truth. The recovered footprints further enable accurate zonal analysis of pedestrian space usage. Finally, we present an ablation study and further compare against state-of-the-art. The proposed foundation substantially outperforms the state-of-the-art across all experiments, achieving an average median DTW of 0.31 m compared to 0.96 m, highlighting the framework's robustness to frequent and prolonged merging and occlusion.</p></details> |  |
| **[RadPose: ISAC-based RF 3D Human Pose Estimation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.01400v1)** | 2026-11-01 | <details><summary>Show</summary><p>Human pose estimation under adverse lighting and occlusion conditions remains challenging for camera- and LiDAR-based systems. Although mmWave radars provide robustness to illumination and occlusion, they rely on dedicated hardware and licensed spectrum, limiting scalability. In this paper, we present RadPose, a learning-based monostatic integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) framework that enables mmWave communication devices to perform 3D human pose estimation. Unlike specialized radars, RadPose leverages monostatic full-duplex operation to extract channel impulse responses (CIRs) directly from standard OFDM communication signals, generating 3D radio point clouds without additional sensing hardware. To address the sparsity and noise of RF observations, RadPose employs a cross-frame transformer-based pose inference network with semantic-guided spatial attention and target-driven temporal attention for robust spatio-temporal aggregation. It further adopts a joint-aware inverse kinematics refinement module based on graph convolution to enforce skeletal topology, bone-length consistency, and anatomical plausibility. Extensive experiments demonstrate RadPose achieves competitive accuracy compared to state-of-the-art radar-based approaches while maintaining robust performance in unseen and occluded scenarios. The dataset and source code are available at https://github.com/Geo-Chou/RadPose.</p></details> | <details><summary>Accep...</summary><p>Accepted to WACV 2027</p></details> |
| **[A Two-Stage Shape- and Motion-Aware Framework for mmWave-based Human Mesh Recovery](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.08530v2)** | 2026-10-27 | <details><summary>Show</summary><p>Millimeter-wave (mmWave) radar has emerged as a promising sensing modality for human perception, offering robustness under challenging environmental conditions and strong privacy preservation. However, recovering accurate 3D human meshes from radar is difficult for two reasons: radar tensors contain significant environmental clutter, and each frame observes only part of the body surface. These challenges demand opposite operations, removing measured energy that does not belong to the body versus inferring geometry the sensor never measured. Yet previous works typically entangle both within a single network, with the mesh objective as the main supervision. We instead reformulate radar-based mesh recovery as two explicitly supervised sub-problems. A signal-level separation stage isolates body-related voxels through coarse-to-fine localization and voxel-wise segmentation, trained with visibility derived voxel labels. A structure-level reconstruction stage then recovers the body from this partial observation using a dual-branch network that jointly models per-frame shape and inter-frame motion. Experiments show that our method reduces mesh error by up to 9.1% over the strongest baseline while using over 10 $\times$ fewer parameters. Source code can be found via https://github.com/haipham03/mmTSM-Mesh</p></details> | accepted by WACV'27 |
| **[3D Occupancy-Language Fields from mmWave Radar](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37929v1)** | 2026-10-27 | <details><summary>Show</summary><p>Radar systems can recover scene geometry and recognize predefined categories, but these outputs do not provide a persistent spatial representation for open-ended language queries. Such queries require linking observations from different viewpoints to the same physical locations. We present TextRadar, a framework that constructs a scene-level 3D occupancy-language field from panoramic radar observations. The field combines occupancy with scale-dependent language features at surface locations, allowing the reconstructed scene to be queried with new descriptions. A single-frame radar distillation model predicts aligned ranges and language features from each radar observation. Using radar-estimated poses, we register these predictions to reconstruct the field from radar alone in a new scene. Experiments on approximately 20k synchronized observations across seven buildings demonstrate scene-level natural-language querying and prompt-free semantic visualization. Analysis of camera-to-radar concept transferability shows stronger agreement for structures, materials, and human poses than for colors and printed text.</p></details> |  |
| **[Soft Temporal Alignment Distillation for Camera-to-mmWave Radar Human Activity Recognition](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36637v1)** | 2026-10-27 | <details><summary>Show</summary><p>Millimeter-wave (mmWave) radar provides privacy?preserving human activity recognition (HAR), but sparse point clouds limit its representation of body structure and motion. We propose a cross-modal knowledge distillation framework in which a teacher trained on camera-derived two-dimensional (2D) human keypoints supervises a radar-only student. The stu?dent combines PointNet-based point-set encoding, bidirectional temporal modeling, segment-level aggregation, and lightweight shared latent-channel scaling. The teacher retains contextualized states at every time step, whereas the student summarizes the radar sequence into a small number of segments, making fixed timestamp correspondence unsuitable for feature transfer. Soft Temporal Alignment Distillation lets each student segment adaptively retrieve and aggregate teacher temporal evidence into its distillation target. Alignment denotes student-conditioned representation-space matching rather than chronological or monotonic registration. On the Multi-Modal Non-Intrusive 4D Human Dataset (MM-Fi), the method improves radar-only ac?curacy from 87.04% to 89.17%, achieving the highest mean accuracy among the evaluated established and recent distillation baselines. It also obtains higher mean accuracy and macro?averaged F1 score (macro-F1) than the radar student under most evaluated point- and frame-dropout settings. Adaptation to our independently collected millimeter-wave Office Human Ac?tivity Recognition Dataset (mmO-HAR) improves accuracy from 80.33% to 87.75%, supporting the transferability of the distilled radar representation. The teacher and alignment branch are removed after training, enabling privacy-preserving radar-only inference without additional sensing or computational branches.</p></details> | 13 pages, 7 figures |
| **[RadarCom: Unlocking Simultaneous Communication and Sensing on Commodity Automotive mmWave Radars](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36622v1)** | 2026-10-27 | <details><summary>Show</summary><p>Vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) communication can improve road safety and traffic efficiency, yet its deployment remains limited by the need for dedicated communication hardware and supporting infrastructure. Meanwhile, production vehicles are already widely equipped with millimeter-wave radars for sensing. To unlock their communication potential, this paper presents RadarCom, a software-defined system that enables direct radar-to-radar communication on unmodified commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) automotive mmWave radars while preserving their native sensing functionality. The key insight is that mutual inter-radar interference, traditionally viewed as harmful, can be repurposed as a communication carrier. Based on this insight, RadarCom introduces slope-mismatch-based discovery, adaptive chirp synchronization, differential coding on range-FFT, and sensing-aware interference suppression to enable simultaneous communication and sensing without hardware modification, waveform redesign, or infrastructure support. We implement RadarCom on TI AWR2243 automotive radars and evaluate it under static, dynamic, and challenging real-world conditions. Results show an average effective data rate of 5.55 kbps with symbol error rates below 1.5%, while maintaining sensing F1 scores of up to 80.5% during concurrent communication. These results demonstrate the feasibility of transforming commodity automotive radars into dual-purpose communication and sensing devices.</p></details> | <details><summary>Accep...</summary><p>Accepted to ACM SenSys 2027. 14 pages</p></details> |
| **[Doppler-aided Position-Velocity Tracking of Hidden Objects using mmWave Radar](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.34085v1)** | 2026-10-25 | <details><summary>Show</summary><p>Safe indoor operation requires autonomous tracking of objects that are not directly visible to the robot. Optical non-line-of-sight (NLoS) methods depend on ambient lighting and scene geometry or on weak multi-bounce returns that need long acquisitions. Millimeter-wave (mmWave) radar offers an attractive alternative: walls act as reflectors for mmWave signals, and frequency-modulated continuous-wave (FMCW) radars enable fast, practical measurement of range, angle, and velocity. However, the low resolution of these radars leads to spatially ambiguous observations. The Doppler information, although particularly sensitive to target motion, remains underexplored in indoor NLoS localization: existing methods emphasize spatial representations and either collapse or discard the Doppler dimension before learning. To leverage the complete Range-Azimuth-Doppler (RAD) information, we acquire the first indoor NLoS radar dataset that pairs sequential RAD measurements with synchronized position and velocity ground truth under controlled variations in motion: 576 sequences totaling 720,856 frames across 12 trajectories of a mobile robot moving along varying speeds, starting positions, and material configurations. We then formulate NLoS tracking as sequential position-velocity estimation rather than frame-wise localization: a shared 3-D encoder processes the full RAD representation of consecutive frames, separate recurrent branches estimate position and velocity, and post-inference refinement combines the two into a motion-consistent trajectory. Our method achieves 8.95cm position and 1.75cm/s velocity errors on held-out trajectories and generalizes to unseen scenarios involving a moving human target. Together, our dataset and tracker establish a benchmark for tracking hidden moving targets with a low-cost radar.</p></details> | 8 pages, 8 figures |
| **[FreqPKC: Frequency-Aware PeakConv for Radar Semantic Segmentation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.33504v1)** | 2026-10-24 | <details><summary>Show</summary><p>Automotive millimeter-wave (mmWave) radar has attracted increasing attention for semantic segmentation in autonomous driving, owing to its robustness under adverse weather and lighting conditions. Recent works have introduced radar-specific neural operators such as PeakConv (PKC), inspired by constant false alarm rate (CFAR) detection, to better model the peak-dominated characteristics of radar images. However, existing methods typically treat the guard bandwidth as learnable parameters, without explicitly characterizing the frequency response of the PKC operator. In this work, we revisit PKC from a frequency-domain perspective and propose Frequency-Aware PeakConv (FreqPKC), which explicitly models and exploits its underlying spectral characteristics. By analyzing the frequency response of PKC, FreqPKC enables the network to capture a broader range of frequency components and adaptively adjust its effective bandwidth. With the proposed Frequency-Aware (FA) module, the network can infer appropriate guard bandwidths to balance high- and low-frequency information: it enhances high-frequency components in target regions for more precise segmentation while suppressing noise through low-frequency filtering in background areas. Building on FreqPKC, we further develop FreqPKC-Net, a radar semantic segmentation (RSS) framework that integrates frequency-guided adaptive modulation with cross-view fusion for multi-view inputs, and can also be adapted to single-view data. Experiments on the public datasets CARRADA, CARRADA-RAC, and a self-built dataset named RS-SAR demonstrate that FreqPKC-Net consistently outperforms existing SoTA methods on both range-Doppler and range-angle views.</p></details> |  |
| **[ICASSP 2026 Radar Acoustic Speech Enhancement (RASE) Challenge](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32202v1)** | 2026-10-23 | <details><summary>Show</summary><p>This paper presents the ICASSP 2026 Radar Acoustic Speech Enhancement (RASE) Grand Challenge, the first community challenge dedicated to benchmarking speech enhancement from millimeter-wave (mmWave) radar vibrometry. Author-accepted manuscript. Challenge resources and code available via the official project website</p></details> |
| **[Radar-Based 3D Human Pose Estimation via Motion-Aware Pose Initialization and Observation-Guided Refinement](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.27774v1)** | 2026-10-20 | <details><summary>Show</summary><p>3D Human Pose Estimation (3D HPE) is used in indoor environments, such as smart homes, to analyze human movement and monitor human states. Millimeter-wave (mmWave) radar is suitable for this task because it is robust to lighting variations and does not capture images of human appearance. However, radar observations often provide insufficient information about certain body parts or contain overlapping reflections from multiple body parts, limiting accurate 3D joint localization. To address these limitations, we propose the Initialization-to-Refinement Pose Framework (I2R-Pose), comprising two stages: Motion-Aware Pose Initialization and Observation-Guided Refinement. In the first stage, joint-wise features are learned by incorporating temporal relationships across consecutive radar observations and human skeletal structure to compensate for insufficient joint information and estimate an initial 3D pose sequence. In the second stage, separately extracted radar observation features predict joint-wise positional corrections that refine the initial pose and generate the final pose sequence. The framework supports individual and fused inputs of time-Doppler/time-range (TD/TR) maps and radar point clouds (PCs). To evaluate performance across indoor activities, we construct the Radar Motion and Spatial Information for 3D Human Pose Estimation (RaMoS-Pose) dataset, providing synchronized TD/TR maps, radar PCs, and 3D joint ground truth (GT). Evaluations on RaMoS-Pose and the publicly available MVDoppler-Pose dataset show that I2R-Pose reduces mean per-joint position error (MPJPE) by 39.50% on MVDoppler-Pose and by 15.13% on RaMoS-Pose with fused inputs, compared with the best-performing existing methods evaluated on each dataset.</p></details> | <details><summary>15 pa...</summary><p>15 pages, 5 figures, 8 tables</p></details> |
| **[mmHand: Toward Pixel-Level-Accuracy Hand Localization Using a Single Commodity mmWave Device](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.05404v1)** | 2026-10-20 | <details><summary>Show</summary><p>The hand localization problem has been a longstanding focus due to its many applications. The task involves modeling the hand as a singular point and determining its position within a defined coordinate system. However, due to data modality limitations, existing hand localization technologies face several challenges. For example, vision-based localization raises privacy concerns, while wearable-based methods compromise user comfort. In this paper, we introduce mmHand, a new device-free, privacy-preserving dynamic hand localization system with pixel-level accuracy, using a single commodity mmWave device. We first propose a mmImage generation tool to fully extract spatial information from raw mmWave data and introduce a novel 2D image-format representation of mmWave data. Next, we design a framework that provides a new quality evaluation method and pixel space labeling for the mmWave data. Finally, we present a cross-modality spatial feature-enhanced model with high spatial feature extraction capabilities, which can accurately localize hand positions at the pixel level in the mmWave radar U-V pixel coordinate system. We evaluate the system with experiments on 12 subjects in three scenarios, and the results across four metrics demonstrate the effectiveness of our hand localization system.</p></details> |  |
| **[mmPencil: Toward Writing-Style-Independent In-Air Handwriting Recognition via mmWave Radar and Large Vision-Language Model](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23419v1)** | 2026-10-16 | <details><summary>Show</summary><p>In-air handwriting recognition based on radio frequency (RF) signals offers a promising solution for human-computer interaction, yet existing methods are often limited by predefined writing planes, constrained writing styles, and small recognition vocabularies. To address these limitations, we propose m^2VLMs, a modality mapping architecture that bridges millimeter-wave (mmWave) radar sensing and large vision-language models (VLMs), and develop mmPencil, a 3D in-air handwriting word recognition system. mmPencil reconstructs 3D handwriting trajectories from mmWave signals using a multi-stage spatial trajectory reconstruction algorithm and maps them into visual representations through a spatial-to-visual mapping algorithm, enabling VLMs to recognize handwriting while reducing sensitivity to writing styles and environmental factors. Extensive experiments demonstrate that mmPencil achieves robust word recognition under variations in writing position, range, angle, speed, size, direction, and user movement. It achieves 97.60% accuracy on 200 word classes for seen users and 92.50% zero-shot accuracy on 50 word classes for unseen users, outperforming state-of-the-art baselines.</p></details> | <details><summary>Publi...</summary><p>Published in ACM IMWUT, Vol. 9, No. 3, Article 81, 2025; presented at ACM UbiComp 2025. 30 pages</p></details> |
| **[FedHUG: Federated Heterogeneous Unsupervised Generalization for Remote Physiological Measurements](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.12132v3)** | 2026-10-09 | <details><summary>Show</summary><p>Remote physiological measurement gained wide attention, while it requires collecting users' privacy-sensitive information, and existing contactless measurements still rely on labeled client data. Subsequently, the \textbf{Fed}erated \textbf{H}eterogeneous \textbf{U}nsupervised \textbf{G}eneralization (\textbf{FedHUG}) framework is proposed and consists of: (1) Minimal Bias Aggregation module dynamically adjusts aggregation weights based on prior-driven bias evaluation to cope with heterogeneous non-IID features from multiple domains. | **[Kapture: Capturing Cardiac Dynamics with Koopman-Governed Learning for Efficient Radar-Based Electrocardiogram Recovery](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.04955v1)** | 2026-10-04 | <details><summary>Show</summary><p>Millimeter-wave (mmWave) radar enables unobtrusive, contactless electrocardiogram (ECG) reconstruction for cardiac monitoring. The Koopman-predicted observables refine subsequent hidden states for ECG reconstruction. The compact configuration approaches the full-width reference accuracy with 68.1% fewer parameters and 91.3% fewer profiler-covered floating-point operations (FLOPs), while the full-width configuration delivers the strongest overall reconstruction performance. Our code will be made publicly available after potential publication.</p></details> | <details><summary>5 pag...</summary><p>5 pages, 3 figures, 2 tables</p></details> |
| **[Learning to Assess Heartbeat Observability for mmWave Heart-Rate Sensing](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.03570v1)** | 2026-10-02 | <details><summary>Show</summary><p>Contactless heart-rate sensing with millimeter-wave (mmWave) radar requires assessing whether individual measurements support reliable estimation. Project page: https://yuxuanhu9.github.io/HEAR/.</p></details> | <details><summary>19 pa...</summary><p>19 pages, 11 figures. Project page: https://yuxuanhu9.github.io/HEAR/</p></details> |
| **[Kinematics-Induced Multimodal 3D Human Pose Estimation with Subject-Level Privacy](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02943v1)** | 2026-10-02 | <details><summary>Show</summary><p>Multimodal 3D Human Pose Estimation (3D HPE) combines complementary information from RGB, LiDAR, and mmWave radar, but models trained on correlated observations from the same individuals, raise privacy risks overlooked by record level analysis. | **[DiFF: Doppler-informed Flow Matching for Human Motion Flow](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.39098v1)** | 2026-09-30 | <details><summary>Show</summary><p>Perceiving human motion via privacy-preserving 4D millimeter-wave (mmWave) radar is critical for next-generation human-robot interaction (HRI), where point cloud scene flow serves as a foundational motion representation. Experiments on an open-source dataset and a self-collected dataset show Equi-RO outperforms state-of-the-art algorithms in accuracy and robustness. Overall, our method achieves 10.7% and 13.4% relative improvements in translation and rotation accuracy, respectively, compared to the best baseline on the open-source dataset.</p></details> |  |
| **[A Lightweight Model-Driven 4D Radar Framework for Pervasive Human Detection in Harsh Conditions](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.13373v1)** | 2026-01-19 | <details><summary>Show</summary><p>Pervasive sensing in industrial and underground environments is severely constrained by airborne dust, smoke, confined geometry, and metallic structures, which rapidly degrade optical and LiDAR based perception. The system uses radar as its sole perception modality and integrates domain aware multi threshold filtering, ego motion compensated temporal accumulation, KD tree Euclidean clustering with Doppler aware refinement, and a rule based 3D classifier. The framework is evaluated in a dust filled enclosed trailer and in real underground mining tunnels, and in the tested scenarios the radar based detector maintains stable pedestrian identification as camera and LiDAR modalities fail under severe visibility degradation. These results suggest that the proposed model-driven approach provides robust, interpretable, and computationally efficient perception for safety-critical applications in harsh industrial and subterranean environments.</p></details> |  |
| **[Real-Time 4D Radar Perception for Robust Human Detection in Harsh Enclosed Environments](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.13364v1)** | 2026-01-19 | <details><summary>Show</summary><p>This paper introduces a novel methodology for generating controlled, multi-level dust concentrations in a highly cluttered environment representative of harsh, enclosed environments, such as underground mines, road tunnels, or collapsed buildings, enabling repeatable mm-wave propagation studies under severe electromagnetic constraints. Building on the filtered point clouds, a cluster-level, rule-based classification pipeline exploits radar semantics-velocity, RCS, and volumetric spread-to achieve reliable, real-time pedestrian detection without extensive domainspecific training. Experimental results confirm that this integrated approach significantly enhances clutter mitigation, detection robustness, and overall system resilience in dust-laden mining environments.</p></details> |  |
| **[Wavelet-based Multi-View Fusion of 4D Radar Tensor and Camera for Robust 3D Object Detection](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.22972v2)** | 2026-01-15 | <details><summary>Show</summary><p>4D millimeter-wave (mmWave) radar has been widely adopted in autonomous driving and robot perception due to its low cost and all-weather robustness. (2) A Geometry-guided Progressive Fusion mechanism, a two-stage query-based fusion strategy that progressively aligns multi-view radar and visual features through geometric priors, enabling modality-agnostic and efficient integration without overwhelming computational overhead. | **[ZK-SenseLM: Verifiable Large-Model Wireless Sensing with Selective Abstention and Zero-Knowledge Attestation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.25677v3)** | 2026-01-14 | <details><summary>Show</summary><p>ZK-SenseLM is a secure and auditable wireless sensing framework that pairs a large-model encoder for Wi-Fi channel state information (and optionally mmWave radar or RFID) with a policy-grounded decision layer and end-to-end zero-knowledge proofs of inference. Furthermore, cross-scenes and cross-datasets experiments confirm PPPR's noise decoupling capability: models trained with PPPR maintain stable performance across diverse furniture arrangements and different radar chipsets, demonstrating its promising generalization capability in the challenging cross-dataset settings. | **[milliMamba: Specular-Aware Human Pose Estimation via Dual mmWave Radar with Multi-Frame Mamba Fusion](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.20128v1)** | 2025-12-23 | <details><summary>Show</summary><p>Millimeter-wave radar offers a privacy-preserving and lighting-invariant alternative to RGB sensors for Human Pose Estimation (HPE) task. Specifically, given the high dimensionality of radar inputs, we adopt a Cross-View Fusion Mamba encoder to efficiently extract spatio-temporal features from longer sequences with linear complexity. A Spatio-Temporal-Cross Attention decoder then predicts joint coordinates across multiple frames. Experiments on the TransHuPR and HuPR datasets demonstrate that our method achieves significant performance improvements, exceeding the baselines by 11.0 AP and 14.6 AP, respectively, while maintaining reasonable complexity. Comprehensive evaluation of preprocessing, data augmentation, and transfer learning for cross-environment generalization in deep learning-based mmWave radar sensing</p></details> |

Specifically, we designed a star graph to describe the high-dimensional relative relationship between a manually added static center point and the dynamic mmWave radar points in the same and consecutive frames. We then adopted DDGNN to learn the features residing in the star graph with variable sizes. Experimental results demonstrated that our approach outperformed other baseline methods using real-world HAR datasets. Our system achieved an overall classification accuracy of 94.27\%, which gets the near-optimal performance with a vision-based skeleton data accuracy of 97.25\%. We also conducted an inference test on Raspberry Pi~4 to demonstrate its effectiveness on resource-constraint platforms. \sh{ We provided a comprehensive ablation study for variable DDGNN structures to validate our model design. Our system also outperformed three recent radar-specific methods without requiring resampling or frame aggregators.</p></details> |  |
| **[mmCounter: Static People Counting in Dense Indoor Scenarios Using mmWave Radar](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.10357v1)** | 2025-12-11 | <details><summary>Show</summary><p>mmWave radars struggle to detect or count individuals in dense, static (non-moving) groups due to limitations in spatial resolution and reliance on movement for detection. In contrast, mmCounter utilizes a novel multi-stage signal processing pipeline to extract relevant low-frequency sources along with their spatial information and map these sources to individual people, enabling accurate counting. Extensive evaluations in various environments demonstrate that mmCounter delivers an 87% average F1 score and 0.6 mean absolute error in familiar environments, and a 60% average F1 score and 1.1 mean absolute error in previously untested environments. | **[mmWEAVER: Environment-Specific mmWave Signal Synthesis from a Photo and Activity Description](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.11894v1)** | 2025-12-10 | <details><summary>Show</summary><p>Realistic signal generation and dataset augmentation are essential for advancing mmWave radar applications such as activity recognition and pose estimation, which rely heavily on diverse, and environment-specific signal datasets. By conditioning on these semantic and geometric priors, mmWeaver generates diverse I/Q signals at multiple resolutions, preserving phase information critical for downstream tasks such as point cloud estimation and activity classification. Extensive experiments show that mmWeaver achieves a complex SSIM of 0.88 and a PSNR of 35 dB, outperforming existing methods in signal realism while improving activity recognition accuracy by up to 7% and reducing human pose estimation error by up to 15%, all while operating 6-35 times faster than simulation-based approaches.</p></details> | <details><summary>Accep...</summary><p>Accepted at the IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision 2026 (WACV 2026)</p></details> |
| **[Who Speaks What from Afar: Eavesdropping In-Person Conversations via mmWave Sensing](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.09285v1)** | 2025-12-10 | <details><summary>Show</summary><p>Multi-participant meetings occur across various domains, such as business negotiations and medical consultations, during which sensitive information like trade secrets, business strategies, and patient conditions is often discussed. Previous research has demonstrated that attackers with mmWave radars outside the room can overhear meeting content by detecting minute speech-induced vibrations on objects. However, these eavesdropping attacks cannot differentiate which speech content comes from which person in a multi-participant meeting, leading to potential misunderstandings and poor decision-making. In this paper, we answer the question ``who speaks what''. By leveraging the spatial diversity introduced by ubiquitous objects, we propose an attack system that enables attackers to remotely eavesdrop on in-person conversations without requiring prior knowledge, such as identities, the number of participants, or seating arrangements. Since participants in in-person meetings are typically seated at different locations, their speech induces distinct vibration patterns on nearby objects. To exploit this, we design a noise-robust unsupervised approach for distinguishing participants by detecting speech-induced vibration differences in the frequency domain. Meanwhile, a deep learning-based framework is explored to combine signals from objects for speech quality enhancement. We validate the proof-of-concept attack on speech classification and signal enhancement through extensive experiments. The experimental results show that our attack can achieve the speech classification accuracy of up to $0.99$ with several participants in a meeting room. Meanwhile, our attack demonstrates consistent speech quality enhancement across all real-world scenarios, including different distances between the radar and the objects.</p></details> |  |
| **[The Evolving Landscape of Interactive Surface Sensing Technologies](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.05071v1)** | 2025-12-04 | <details><summary>Show</summary><p>Interactive surfaces have evolved from capacitive touch and IR based systems into a diverse ecosystem of sensing technologies that support rich and expressive human computer interaction. This survey traces that progression, beginning with infrared vision based approaches, such as FTIR and diffuse illumination, and the rise of capacitive touch as the dominant technology in modern devices, to focusing on contemporary modalities including vision and acoustic sensing. New technologies under development are also discussed, including mmWave radar, and vibration based techniques. Each sensing technique is examined in terms of its operating principles, resolution, scalability, and applications, along with discussions of multimodal integration. By comparing tradeoffs between sensing modalities, the survey highlights the technical and design factors that shape interactive surface performance and user experience. The review concludes by identifying persistent challenges, including sensing accuracy, power constraints, and privacy concerns, and outlines how emerging sensing modalities can enable future interactive environments to be ubiquitous and intelligent.</p></details> | 12 pages, 10 figures |
| **[mmPred: Radar-based Human Motion Prediction in the Dark](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.00345v1)** | 2025-11-29 | <details><summary>Show</summary><p>Existing Human Motion Prediction (HMP) methods based on RGB-D cameras are sensitive to lighting conditions and raise privacy concerns, limiting their real-world applications such as firefighting and healthcare. Motivated by the robustness and privacy-preserving nature of millimeter-wave (mmWave) radar, this work introduces radar as a novel sensing modality for HMP, for the first time. Nevertheless, radar signals often suffer from specular reflections and multipath effects, resulting in noisy and temporally inconsistent measurements, such as body-part miss-detection. To address these radar-specific artifacts, we propose mmPred, the first diffusion-based framework tailored for radar-based HMP. mmPred introduces a dual-domain historical motion representation to guide the generation process, combining a Time-domain Pose Refinement (TPR) branch for learning fine-grained details and a Frequency-domain Dominant Motion (FDM) branch for capturing global motion trends and suppressing frame-level inconsistency. Furthermore, we design a Global Skeleton-relational Transformer (GST) as the diffusion backbone to model global inter-joint cooperation, enabling corrupted joints to dynamically aggregate information from others. Extensive experiments show that mmPred achieves state-of-the-art performance, outperforming existing methods by 8.6% on mmBody and 22% on mm-Fi.</p></details> | <details><summary>This ...</summary><p>This paper is accepted by AAAI-2026</p></details> |
| **[Design and Measurements of mmWave FMCW Radar Based Non-Contact Multi-Patient Heart Rate and Breath Rate Monitoring System](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.21255v2)** | 2025-11-28 | <details><summary>Show</summary><p>Recent developments in mmWave radar technologies have enabled the truly non-contact heart-rate (HR) and breath-rate (BR) measurement approaches, which provides a great ease in patient monitoring. In this work, a frequency modulated continuous wave (FMCW) mmWave radar based truly non-contact multiple patient HR and BR monitoring system has been presented. Furthermore, a novel approach is also proposed, which combines multiple processing methods using a least squares solution to improve measurement accuracy, generalization, and handle measurement error. The proposed system has been developed using Texas Instruments' FMCW radar and experimental results with multiple subjects are also presented, which show >97% and >93% accuracy in the measured BR and HR values, respectively.</p></details> | <details><summary>Prese...</summary><p>Presented at BioCAS 2023</p></details> |

| **[4D Point Splatting for mmWave Radar Micro-Doppler Differentiable Rendering](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.08342v1)** | 2026-11-05 | <details><summary>Show</summary><p>Millimeter-wave radar resolves the micrometer displacements of a moving body as micro-Doppler, enabling gait, gesture, activity, pose and vital-sign sensing. Each task relies on a downstream model trained on real data, yet radar datasets lag orders of magnitude behind vision and language. Brute-force collection will not close that gap, and existing synthesis methods (forward-only simulators, learned generators and static-scene inverse renderers) cannot fit a real capture of a moving body, leaving a sim2real gap. We present 4D Point Splatting (4DPS), a physics-based differentiable renderer that fits an explicit moving scene to a real capture. Using the synchronized camera to initialize the room and body, we represent the scene as oriented points carrying material, normal and velocity, and splat each point into range and Doppler bins. Our output is the raw complex return a real radar records, so we apply the same signal processing on the rendered data to obtain any representation for training any SOTA downstream model. We fit 235 sequences on HuPR and 100 on RT-Pose, two datasets with different radars. Our reconstructions set the state of the art, with median correlations of 0.940 and 0.830 on range-azimuth, 0.829 and 0.695 on range-Doppler, and 0.988 and 0.966 on micro-Doppler. Our renders also set the state of the art in downstream sim2real gap. On RT-Pose, a pose model trained on them reaches 21.9 cm MPJPE on real data, against 16.7 cm for real training and 127.6 cm for the RF-Genesis baseline, where both the rendered- and real-trained models learn nearly the same features. Our custom CUDA kernels fit a sequence in 5.7 minutes on HuPR and 12.9 on RT-Pose on one H100, making dataset-scale inverse rendering of mmWave radar possible for the first time. This work can enable synthetic data generation for any human-centered downstream task and model, and scene editing for data augmentation.</p></details> | Under Review |

Yet existing radar methods remain deterministic, collapsing this ambiguity into a single estimate. Diffusion-based alternatives can model multi-hypothesis distributions but require costly sequential denoising for each sample and lack calibrated uncertainty. We propose Multi-Hypothesis Normalizing Flow Pose Generator (MH-NFPG), which models pose distributions from radar point clouds using a conditional normalizing flow. Specifically, we combine a spatiotemporal transformer backbone with a normalizing flow that transforms a Laplace base distribution into an expressive posterior, generated in parallel through a single forward pass. Leveraging this efficiency, we outperform diffusion-based alternatives in calibration across three radar benchmarks (MM-Fi, mmRadPose, mRI) at comparable pose accuracy, while achieving up to 22x faster inference and reducing calibration error by up to 84%. We find that calibration degrades substantially for diffusion models, whereas our flow-based approach maintains reliable coverage, also across environments. These results demonstrate normalizing flows as a practical alternative to diffusion models for real-time, uncertainty-aware radar pose estimation. Our code is available at https://github.com/jonasmueler/YouOnlyFlowOnce_WACV.</p></details> | <details><summary>Accep...</summary><p>Accepted at the Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision (WACV) 2027</p></details> |

The key insight is that mutual inter-radar interference, traditionally viewed as harmful, can be repurposed as a communication carrier. Based on this insight, RadarCom introduces slope-mismatch-based discovery, adaptive chirp synchronization, differential coding on range-FFT, and sensing-aware interference suppression to enable simultaneous communication and sensing without hardware modification, waveform redesign, or infrastructure support. However, transplanting 3D Gaussian splatting to coherent sensing fails by construction; Gaussian splats discard the sidelobe energy (10-20% of the total) and the phase that governs coherent interference between reflectors. Our key idea is to replace the learned Gaussian footprint with the physically exact Dirichlet kernel of the finite-window DFT, modulated by a surfel that carries area, normal, and material, so that the rendering primitive matches the measurement physics instead of approximating it. We pair this primitive with a specialized solver, Dirichlet Sliding Frank-Wolfe (DSFW), that combines variable projection, residual dual certificates, and certificate-driven hard replacement of low-utility surfels, with periodic low-resolution coupled Levenberg-Marquardt correction, navigating the rugged loss landscape that breaks generic first-order optimizers. Accepted for publication in ACM Transactions on Graphics</p></details> |
| **[mmHRI: Towards Privacy-Preserving Human-Robot Interaction with Millimeter-Wave Radar](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.34220v2)** | 2026-09-30 | <details><summary>Show</summary><p>Assistive robots increasingly operate in many human-centered environments and perform various human-robot interaction (HRI) tasks, such as object delivery. Since this calibration is irreversible, it uses only loop closures accepted by the mapping graph and a cycle-consistency test. Extensive evaluations demonstrate high accuracy and drift-reduced estimation at real-time speeds.</p></details> | 8 pages, 8 figures |
| **[4D Radar Perception Algorithms for Autonomous Driving: A Review](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.19216v1)** | 2026-09-16 | <details><summary>Show</summary><p>Research on 4D millimeter-wave radar perception algorithms has flourished in recent years, extending from signal processing and object detection to semantic segmentation, motion estimation, occupancy prediction, and dynamic scene reconstruction. This review organizes the field according to the evolution of perception tasks and algorithms. Across these directions, we compare radar-only learning, multimodal fusion, and cross-modal supervision and knowledge distillation. Particular attention is paid to how elevation, Doppler measurements, and radar physical priors are exploited across tasks. We further summarize the task coverage, input data, annotations, and evaluation protocols of existing datasets, clarifying the empirical support for different research directions. Finally, we discuss the common challenges and future directions of 4D radar perception for autonomous driving. This review provides a task-oriented perspective on the transition from sparse object perception to dynamic spatial understanding.</p></details> | <details><summary>12 pa...</summary><p>12 pages, 9 figures, 5 tables. Submitted to IEEE Sensors Journal</p></details> |

To fill this gap, we make the key observation that latent diffusion models (LDMs), though successful in other modalities, have not been effectively leveraged for radar-based 3D generation due to a lack of compatible representations and conditioning strategies. We introduce RaLD, a framework that bridges this gap by integrating scene-level frustum-based LiDAR autoencoding, order-invariant latent representations, and direct radar spectrum conditioning. These insights lead to a more compact and expressive generation process. Moreover, the velocity dimension of 4D radar provides motion cues that help anchor and refine the spatial distribution of Gaussians. Specifically, RaGS adopts a cascaded pipeline to construct and progressively refine the Gaussian field. It begins with Frustum-based Localization Initiation (FLI), which unprojects foreground pixels to initialize coarse Gaussian centers. Then, Iterative Multimodal Aggregation (IMA) explicitly exploits image semantics and implicitly integrates 4D radar velocity geometry to refine the Gaussians within regions of interest. Finally, Multi-level Gaussian Fusion (MGF) renders the Gaussian field into hierarchical BEV features for 3D object detection. By dynamically focusing on sparse and informative regions, RaGS achieves object-centric precision and comprehensive scene perception.
